states.narration: Both terms count copies of the same whole quantity x+y, even though neither contribution is a known number.
Add the counts while preserving the shared group. Neither x nor y changes.
There are six copies of the whole group. Each copy contains both x and y.
Each contribution receives the same factor six. There is no constant product to evaluate; the reasoning ends here.

editorial.title: What if both contributions are unknown?
editorial.setup: Treat x+y as a whole quantity, then follow its two contributions as six copies are opened.
editorial.summary: Counting the whole group and counting each contribution give the same value. Neither contribution needs a known numerical value.
